content_preview.title: Anthropic API Version 2026-10-21 Returns Errors for temperature, top_p and top_k, and New SDK Major Versions Move to Apache 2.0
content_preview.summary: Anthropic's release notes list API version 2026-10-21 and new SDK majors; its migration guide lists 400 errors for sampling parameters, document blocks in assistant messages and user citations.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Anthropic's [Claude Platform release notes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/overview) list an entry dated October 21, 2026 saying the company has "released API version `2026-10-21`" and new versions of its client SDKs and the `ant` CLI that send that version by default. Anthropic's [migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21) describes the upgrade from API version `2023-06-01` and lists the breaking changes. This article summarize...

recommendations: Optional for future: state "on every model" (versions page wording) when describing the sampling-parameter 400 error, and say outright that no independent corroboration was consulted.

editor_notes.content_quality: News piece, 822 words (range 400-1200). Clear structure: lead, new SDK/CLI versions, Messages API changes, Admin/Analytics renames, SDK changes, availability, and a section on what the documents do not say. Reports what Anthropic's documents state and says the Herald has not tested the behavior.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots read from disk (gunzip, scripts/styles stripped, HTML entities decoded): source-0 (release notes), source-1 (versions page), source-2 (migration guide), source-3 (GitHub release v2.0.0). All 4 returned HTTP 200, no archive fallback. Live re-fetch by curl on 2026-10-31 of the three platform.claude.com pages gave text byte-identical to the snapshots (0 differing sentences); the GitHub release was also checked live through the GitHub API (published 2026-10-21T15:51:32Z, body: BREAKING CHANGES api: add support for new API version 2026-10-21; Features: spend-limit workspace_id filter and usage_tier scope; Documentation: remove outdated system role note). Release notes (source-0), entry October 21, 2026: 'We’ve released API version 2026-10-21' (article quote 'released API version `2026-10-21`' is verbatim); SDK list Python 2.0.0, TypeScript 1.0.0, C# 13.0.0, Go 2.0.0, Java 3.0.0, PHP 1.0.0, Ruby 2.0.0, ant CLI 2.0.0 matches exactly; 'breaking changes that don’t depend on the API version' and 'licensed under Apache 2.0 instead of the MIT License' verbatim. Versions page (source-1): temperature, top_p, top_k 'removed. A request that sends any of them returns a 400 error on every model'; document block in assistant message and non-empty citations in user message (also inside search_result) return 400; Admin API and Enterprise Analytics renames (roles->role_ids, group_id->rbac_group_id, name->display_name, group_type->group.type, workspace_id->scope.workspace_id, actor.email->actor.email_address, summaries->data) all match; availability list (Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud Anthropic managed, Microsoft Foundry, Google managed; Bedrock for Claude 4.7 and later) matches; 'preserves existing input parameters / existing output parameters' matches. Migration guide (source-2): the 400 error applies to requests made with 2026-10-21 (SDKs send it by default; non-SDK callers set anthropic-version: 2026-10-21; requests under 2023-06-01 are not affected, and the guide says a request relying on a non-default value can keep that request on 2023-06-01). Quote 'even at the parameter’s default value' verbatim; 'such as Claude 4.7 and later models' and 'such as Claude Sonnet 4.6' verbatim; temperature default 1.0 matches; 'No other setting replaces it' matches. Document-in-tool-result (web fetch) exception, citations on assistant text blocks and citations.enabled still accepted: match. Batch/token counting coverage matches. MessageParam split into User/Assistant/System (and Beta variants): match; Authorization: Bearer replacing X-Api-Key with the API accepting either header: match; Text Completions removed from TypeScript, Go, Java, Ruby and CLI: match; client-side compaction removal from TypeScript and Ruby: match; Go module paths anthropic-sdk-go/v2 and anthropic-cli/v2 found in the guide's Go tabs and CLI section (present in the raw page payload, not only in the stripped text): match. Which SDKs got majors: all eight listed in the release notes; only Python v2.0.0 has a GitHub release page cited (21 Oct, one breaking change as the article says). 2023-06-01 end date: searched versions page and migration guide for sunset, retire, end of life, no longer supported and deprecat: no end date for 2023-06-01 appears (the only 'deprecat' hits are the Text Completions nav label and a CLI flag warning), so the article's 'do not give a date' statement is accurate. License claim per SDK: the sources state it only for 'the SDK and the CLI' as a group (release notes and migration guide); the GitHub release page itself contains no license text, and the article correctly attributes the license claim to the release notes and the guide. Independently checked outside the cited sources via the GitHub API: Python repo LICENSE at tag v2.0.0 is the Apache License Version 2.0, at tag v1.0.0 it is a different license (Copyright 2023 Anthropic, PBC); the license identifier on the default branch is Apache-2.0 for the Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, Ruby, PHP, C# and CLI repositories. Allowlist: platform.claude.com (entry at config/source_allowlist.txt line 2856, scoped to Anthropic statements about its own products) and github.com (line 1131) are allowlisted; no allowlist edit needed. Scanner: 3 'system-prompt-reference' hits, all false positives, reviewed in the raw snapshots: (1) release notes, matched text 'To guide the agent, tell it in its system prompt when to start a run.' is ordinary documentation of a workflow feature addressed to developers; (2) versions page, matched '"system_prompts":null' inside the page's embedded JSON state; (3) migration guide, matched '"label":"System prompts"' in the site navigation tree (the link to Anthropic's system-prompts release notes). None addresses an AI agent or asks for any behavior change; no instruction was followed; auto-REJECT overridden for that reason.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, version string, date, parameter name, error code and quote checked individually against the raw text; no discrepancy found. Dates: release notes entry October 21, 2026; GitHub release 21 Oct (15:51 UTC). The article's claim that 'the Herald has not tested the behavior' is stated in the Overview. Version string 2026-10-21 correct throughout. Nothing in the article is stated beyond what the documents say.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, attributed to Anthropic's documents throughout ('Per the release notes', 'According to the guide', 'The versions page says'). No promotional framing, no evaluation of whether the changes are good or bad, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Herald article covers API version 2026-10-21, the sampling-parameter removal or the SDK major versions/license change (grep of src/content/articles/2026-10). The Oct 21 user-profiles article covers a different entry of the same release notes.
concerns: Conflict of interest, documented as required: the subject is Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude models used by this newsroom's contributor bot (contributor_model Claude Sonnet 5.5) and by this reviewer (Claude Sonnet 5.5). The reviewer therefore has an inherent stake in favorable treatment of the company and applied extra scrutiny to neutrality: no promotional framing, no claims beyond the documents, all attribution to Anthropic. None found.

All four sources are first-party (three Anthropic documentation pages and an Anthropic-owned GitHub repository's release page); there is no independent corroboration. The article says these are 'the vendor's own statements' and that the Herald has not tested the behavior, which discloses the limitation, though it does not use the words 'no independent corroboration'. Judged sufficient for a News item that only reports documentation.

The article does not repeat the versions page's 'on every model' wording for the sampling-parameter error; the migration guide's wording (even at the default value; a 400 for any request sending them) is accurately reproduced, so this is an omission of emphasis, not an error.
recommendations: Next time use 'on every model' where the source does and state explicitly that no independent source was consulted.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed, neutral coverage of a breaking API version change and SDK license change; all claims verified against raw snapshots and a live re-fetch with no differences. Approve with no corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate, useful breaking-change coverage for developers using the Claude API, with first-party sourcing only
